events.event: Light is divided from darkness
events.note: The passage shows light created and divided from darkness on the first day.

events.event: The firmament divides the waters
events.note: The passage shows the firmament dividing the waters on the second day.

events.event: Dry land appears and plants grow
events.note: The passage shows dry land appearing and plants growing on the third day.

events.event: The sun, moon and stars are set in the sky
events.note: The passage describes the two great lights and the stars, set in the firmament on the fourth day. The KJV says "greater light" and "lesser light" rather than naming the sun and moon.

events.event: Sea creatures and birds are created
events.note: The passage shows the water creatures and fowl created on the fifth day.

events.event: God tells Noah to build an ark of gopher wood
events.note: Verse 14 gives the command but does not name the speaker. Verse 13 shows that God is speaking to Noah.

events.event: Noah's family and the animals go into the ark
events.note: The current reference fully shows Noah's family and the animals going in.

events.event: Rain falls for forty days and forty nights
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: A dove returns with an olive leaf
events.note: Verse 10 shows Noah sending the dove out again, which gives context for its return with the olive leaf.

events.event: God sets His bow in the cloud as a covenant sign
events.note: Verse 13 contains the bow, but verse 12 shows that God is speaking and introduces the token of the covenant.

events.event: Jacob is born holding Esau's heel
events.note: The verse names Jacob and says his hand took hold of Esau's heel at birth.

events.event: Esau sells his birthright for pottage
events.note: Esau swears away his birthright, and Jacob gives him bread and pottage of lentils.

events.event: Jacob dreams of a ladder to heaven
events.note: Verse 12 alone says only 'he dreamed'. Verses 10-11 identify the dreamer as Jacob.

events.event: Jacob wrestles and is renamed Israel
events.note: Verse 28 gives only the renaming. Verses 24-27 add the wrestling through the night that leads to the new name.

events.event: God calls Abram to leave his country
events.note: The verse directly records the LORD telling Abram to leave his country, kindred and father's house.

events.event: God promises descendants like the stars
events.note: God tells Abram to count the stars and says, 'So shall thy seed be.'

events.event: Abram's name is changed to Abraham
events.note: God explicitly renames Abram as Abraham.

events.event: Isaac is born to Sarah
events.note: Widened to include verse 2, which states that Sarah conceived and bare Abraham a son. Verse 3 adds that he was named Isaac.

events.event: Abraham is tested in the land of Moriah
events.note: Verse 1 is added because it states that God tested ('did tempt') Abraham. Verse 2 names the land of Moriah.

events.event: Jacob gives Joseph a coat of many colours
events.note: Israel (Jacob) makes Joseph a coat of many colours; the verse fully shows the event.

events.event: Joseph's brothers sell him for twenty pieces of silver
events.note: Verse 28 alone is ambiguous about who sold Joseph. Verses 26-27 show Judah proposing the sale and the brothers agreeing, so the passage shows the brothers selling him.

events.event: Joseph serves in Potiphar's house
events.note: Verse 1 shows only the purchase. Verses 2-4 show Joseph living in his Egyptian master's house, serving him and being made overseer.

events.event: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dream
events.note: Verse 25 only opens Joseph's reply. Verses 26-30 give the actual interpretation: seven years of plenty followed by seven years of famine.

events.event: Joseph reveals himself to his brothers
events.note: Joseph declares, 'I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt'; the verse fully shows the event.

events.event: Waters turned to blood
events.note: The current verse fully shows the waters of the river being turned to blood.

events.event: Frogs cover the land
events.note: The current verse fully shows the frogs coming up and covering the land of Egypt.

events.event: Dust becomes lice
events.note: The current verse fully shows the dust becoming lice throughout Egypt.

events.event: Thick darkness for three days
events.note: The current verse fully shows the thick darkness in all the land of Egypt for three days.

events.event: Death of the firstborn
events.note: The current verse fully shows the LORD smiting all the firstborn of Egypt at midnight.

events.event: God provides manna
events.note: Verse 15 names the manna and calls it the bread the LORD has given. Adding verse 14 shows it appearing on the ground.

events.event: The Ten Commandments are given at Sinai
events.note: Exodus 20:3 alone is just one commandment and does not mention Sinai or God speaking. Exodus 19:20 places the LORD on Mount Sinai, and 20:1-3 shows God speaking the commandments.

events.event: The people make a golden calf
events.note: Verse 4 shows the calf being made, but 'he' is unnamed there. Verses 1-3 show the people asking Aaron and bringing their gold, which makes it clear the people were behind it.

events.event: Twelve spies are sent to search Canaan
events.note: Verse 2 gives the command to send one man from each tribe. Verse 3 and verse 17 show Moses actually sending them to spy out Canaan.

events.event: Baby Moses is placed among the bulrushes
events.note: The verse shows Moses' mother placing him in an ark of bulrushes among the flags by the river's brink, which fully shows the event.

events.event: God speaks from the burning bush
events.note: Verse 2 shows only the burning bush. Verse 4 adds that 'God called unto him out of the midst of the bush,' which shows God speaking.

events.event: The river is turned to blood
events.note: The verse states that all the waters in the river were turned to blood, which fully shows the event.

events.event: The first Passover is kept
events.note: Verse 13 is God's instruction, not the keeping of the Passover. Verses 21-23 show Moses telling the elders to kill the passover and strike the blood. Verse 28 shows Israel doing as commanded.

events.event: Israel crosses the Red Sea on dry ground
events.note: The verse shows Israel going into the midst of the sea on dry ground, which fully shows the event.

events.event: An angel appears to Gideon by the winepress
events.note: Fully shows the angel appearing to Gideon as he threshed wheat by the winepress.

events.event: Gideon tests God with a fleece
events.note: Widened to show Gideon's request and God answering both fleece tests (wet fleece, then dry fleece).

events.event: God reduces the army to three hundred
events.note: Widened to include the water test that selected the three hundred who lapped, ending with God's word to Gideon.

events.event: Trumpets sound and pitchers are broken
events.note: Fully shows the three companies blowing trumpets, breaking pitchers, and crying out.

events.event: Rahab hides the spies in Jericho
events.note: Fully shows the event: the spies are sent to Jericho, lodge with Rahab, and she hides them.

events.event: Israel crosses the Jordan on dry ground
events.note: Fully shows the event: all Israel passes over Jordan on dry ground.

events.event: The walls of Jericho fall
events.note: Joshua 6:20 shows the wall falling but only says 'the city'. Joshua 6:1-2 names Jericho.

events.event: The sun stands still at Gibeon
events.note: Widened to include verse 12, which names Gibeon and gives Joshua's command to the sun.

events.event: An angel announces a Nazarite son
events.note: Widened to include verse 3, which shows that the speaker is the angel of the LORD appearing to Manoah's wife. Verse 5 alone does not identify the angel.

events.event: Samson tears a young lion
events.note: The current reference fully shows Samson tearing the young lion.

events.event: Samson loves Delilah
events.note: The current reference names Delilah and states that Samson loved her.

events.event: Samson brings down the house
events.note: The current reference fully shows the house falling on the lords and the people.

events.event: Ruth vows to go with Naomi
events.note: Widened. Verse 16 alone has Ruth speaking only to 'thee'. Verses 14-15 show she is speaking to her mother in law after Orpah leaves. Verses 17-18 complete the vow and show her steadfast resolve to go.

events.event: Ruth gleans in the field of Boaz
events.note: Widened. Verse 3 refers only to 'she'. Verse 2 names Ruth the Moabitess and gives her request to glean.

events.event: Ruth asks Boaz to spread his skirt over her
events.note: Kept. Ruth names herself and makes the request. Boaz is clearly the one addressed in context.

events.event: Boaz marries Ruth
events.note: Kept. The verse explicitly states that Boaz took Ruth as his wife.

events.event: Obed is born
events.note: Kept. The verse says a son is born and names him Obed. It also links him to Jesse and David.

events.event: Hannah prays and makes a vow
events.note: Verse 10 only says 'she', so verse 9 is added to name Hannah.

events.event: The LORD calls the boy Samuel
events.note: Verse 8 calls Samuel 'the child' and shows the repeated call, which completes the event.

events.event: Samuel anoints Saul
events.note: Saul is not named in 10:1; 9:27 names him as the one Samuel took aside.

events.event: Samuel anoints David
events.note: The current reference names both Samuel and David and fully shows the anointing.

events.event: Solomon asks for an understanding heart
events.note: The verse directly records Solomon's request for an understanding heart.

events.event: Solomon judges between two mothers
events.note: 3:25 alone does not show the two women. Adding 3:16-17 introduces the two harlots, and 3:24-27 shows the judgment and its outcome.

events.event: Solomon builds the house of the LORD
events.note: 6:14 says only 'the house'. 6:1 identifies it as the house of the LORD that Solomon began to build.

events.event: The temple is dedicated
events.note: The verse explicitly states that the king and Israel dedicated the house of the LORD.

events.event: The queen of Sheba visits
events.note: 10:1 shows her coming to prove Solomon. 10:2 adds her arrival in Jerusalem, which completes the visit.

events.event: Samuel anoints David
events.note: Keep the current reference. It shows Samuel anointing David among his brothers, and the verse names David.

events.event: David plays the harp for Saul
events.note: Keep the current reference. It shows David playing the harp to refresh Saul.

events.event: David defeats Goliath
events.note: Verse 50 only says 'the Philistine', so 17:4 is added because it names Goliath. Verses 48-50 show the sling, the stone and the victory.

events.event: David spares Saul in the cave
events.note: Verse 4 alone shows only the cutting of Saul's robe. Widened to include the cave (v3) and David refusing to harm Saul or let his men rise against him (v6-7).

events.event: David is anointed king over Israel
events.note: Keep the current reference. It shows the elders anointing David king over Israel at Hebron.

events.event: Daniel refuses the king's meat
events.note: Verse 8 fully shows Daniel purposing not to defile himself with the king's meat and wine.

events.event: Daniel interprets the dream of the great image
events.note: Verse 31 only describes the image. Verses 36-38 show Daniel giving the interpretation, with Nebuchadnezzar as the head of gold.

events.event: Three friends are cast into the furnace
events.note: Widened to include the command to cast them in and verse 21's statement that they 'were cast into the midst of the burning fiery furnace'.

events.event: Fingers write on the palace wall
events.note: Verse 5 fully shows the fingers of a man's hand writing on the plaister of the palace wall.

events.event: Daniel is cast into the den of lions
events.note: Verse 16 fully shows Daniel being cast into the den of lions at the king's command.

events.event: God calls Jonah to go to Nineveh
events.note: Widened to include verse 1, which names Jonah as the one receiving the word of the LORD. Verse 2 alone gives only the command.

events.event: Jonah flees toward Tarshish
events.note: The current reference fully shows Jonah fleeing toward Tarshish by ship from Joppa.

events.event: A great fish swallows Jonah
events.note: The current reference fully shows the LORD preparing a great fish to swallow Jonah.

events.event: Jonah warns Nineveh: forty days
events.note: The current reference fully shows Jonah's warning: 'Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.'

events.event: God prepares a gourd to shade Jonah
events.note: The current reference fully shows God preparing the gourd as a shadow over Jonah's head.

events.event: Esther is made queen
events.note: The verse states that the king set the royal crown on Esther's head and made her queen instead of Vashti.

events.event: Haman plots against the Jews
events.note: The verse states that Haman sought to destroy all the Jews throughout the kingdom.

events.event: Esther goes in to the king
events.note: Verse 1 adds that Esther put on her royal apparel and stood in the inner court of the king's house, which shows her going in. Verse 2 shows the king holding out the sceptre.

events.event: Haman is hanged on his own gallows
events.note: The verse states that Haman was hanged on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai.

events.event: Ravens feed Elijah
events.note: Verse 6 says only 'him'. Verse 1 names Elijah, and verse 4 records God commanding the ravens to feed him.

events.event: The widow's meal and oil do not run out
events.note: Verse 16 does not mention the widow. Verse 9 identifies her as a widow woman of Zarephath, and verse 15 shows her household eating.

events.event: Fire falls on Mount Carmel
events.note: Verse 38 names neither Carmel nor Elijah. Verse 20 names mount Carmel, and verse 36 shows Elijah praying before the fire falls.

events.event: Elijah hears a still small voice
events.note: Verse 12 does not name Elijah. Verse 13 does, and it shows him hearing the voice.

events.event: Elijah goes up by a whirlwind
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Jesus is baptized
events.note: Verse 16 explicitly states Jesus was baptized and came up out of the water, so the current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Jesus is tempted in the wilderness
events.note: Verse 1 explicitly states Jesus was led into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil, so the current reference is sufficient.

events.event: Jesus calls fishermen to be fishers of men
events.note: Verse 19 alone does not show that 'them' are fishermen. Verse 18 identifies Simon Peter and Andrew casting a net, 'for they were fishers', and verse 20 shows them following Jesus.

events.event: Jesus teaches on the mountain
events.note: Verse 1 shows Jesus going up into the mountain but not teaching. Verse 2 adds 'he opened his mouth, and taught them.'

events.event: Crowds cry Hosanna as Jesus enters Jerusalem
events.note: Widened: verse 9 has the Hosanna cry, and verse 10 shows Jesus coming into Jerusalem.

events.event: Jesus breaks bread at the Last Supper
events.note: Kept: the verse fully shows Jesus taking, blessing, breaking and giving the bread.

events.event: Jesus prays in Gethsemane
events.note: Widened: verse 36 names Gethsemane but only announces the prayer; verse 39 shows Jesus actually praying.

events.event: Jesus is crucified
events.note: Kept: the verse states plainly that they crucified him.

events.event: The angel says: He is not here, for he is risen
events.note: Widened: verse 5 shows that the angel is the speaker of the words in verse 6.

events.event: Gabriel announces Jesus' birth to Mary
events.note: Luke 1:31 alone does not name Gabriel or Mary. Verses 26-27 identify the angel Gabriel and the virgin Mary, so the passage is widened to include them.

events.event: Joseph and Mary travel to Bethlehem
events.note: Verse 4 mentions only Joseph. Verse 5 adds that Mary went with him, so it is included.

events.event: Angels appear to shepherds
events.note: Verses 8-9 describe a single angel. The plural 'angels' is shown when the multitude of the heavenly host appears in verse 13, so the passage is widened through verse 14.

events.event: Simeon holds the child in the temple
events.note: The current reference fully shows Simeon in the temple taking the child Jesus up in his arms.

events.event: The twelve-year-old Jesus is found in the temple
events.note: The current reference fully shows Jesus at age twelve being found in the temple after three days.

events.event: The women find the stone rolled away
events.note: Verses 2-3 do not say who 'they' are. Verse 1 adds the visit to the sepulchre with spices, and verse 10 names the women (Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James and others).

events.event: Two disciples walk to Emmaus
events.note: The current reference fully shows two of them going that same day to Emmaus.

events.event: Jesus stands among the disciples: Peace be unto you
events.note: The current reference fully shows Jesus standing in their midst and saying 'Peace be unto you.'

events.event: Jesus is carried up into heaven
events.note: The current reference fully shows Jesus parted from them and carried up into heaven.

events.event: Jesus is taken up in a cloud
events.note: Verse 9 fully shows Jesus being taken up and received by a cloud.

events.event: The Spirit comes at Pentecost
events.note: These verses fully describe the Holy Ghost coming on the day of Pentecost.

events.event: A lame man is healed at the temple gate
events.note: Widened to include verse 2, which places the lame man at the temple gate called Beautiful.

events.event: Stephen is stoned
events.note: Verse 59 explicitly states that they stoned Stephen.

events.event: Saul meets the risen Jesus near Damascus
events.note: Widened to verse 5, where the voice says, 'I am Jesus whom thou persecutest'.

events.event: A traveller falls among thieves
events.note: Verse 30 fully shows the man going down to Jericho and falling among thieves.

events.event: A priest passes by
events.note: Verse 31 shows the priest passing by on the other side.

events.event: A Levite passes by
events.note: Verse 32 shows the Levite passing by on the other side.

events.event: A Samaritan binds up his wounds
events.note: Verses 33-34 name the Samaritan and show him binding up the wounds.

events.event: He pays the host two pence
events.note: Verse 35 shows him giving two pence to the host.

events.event: All the earth has one language
events.note: Verse 1 states this directly.

events.event: People settle in a plain in the land of Shinar
events.note: Verse 2 names the plain in the land of Shinar and says they dwelt there.

events.event: They make brick and plan a city and a tower
events.note: Verses 3-4 cover the brick-making and the plan for a city and a tower.

events.event: The LORD comes down to see the city
events.note: Verse 5 states this directly.

events.event: Their language is confounded and they are scattered
events.note: Verses 7-8 show the confounding and the scattering. Verse 9 is added because it names the place Babel and restates both actions.

events.event: Saul is converted near Damascus
events.note: Verse 3 shows only the light from heaven. Widened to include Saul falling down, hearing Jesus speak, and submitting to him, which shows the conversion itself.

events.event: Barnabas and Saul are separated for the work
events.note: The current verse fully shows the Holy Ghost commanding that Barnabas and Saul be separated for the work.

events.event: Paul sees a vision of a man of Macedonia
events.note: The current verse fully shows the vision of the man of Macedonia.

events.event: Paul preaches on Mars' hill in Athens
events.note: The current verse fully shows Paul speaking on Mars' hill to the men of Athens.

events.event: Paul is shipwrecked on Melita
events.note: Acts 28:1 names Melita but does not describe the shipwreck. Added Acts 27:41-44, where the ship runs aground and breaks up and everyone escapes safely to land.

events.event: The younger son asks for his portion
events.note: Verse 11 introduces the two sons. Verse 12 shows the younger son asking for his portion and the father dividing his living.

events.event: He wastes his substance with riotous living
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: He feeds swine in a far country
events.note: Verse 15 speaks only of 'that country'. Verse 13 identifies it as a far country, and verse 14 explains the famine that led him to feed swine.

events.event: His father runs to embrace him
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: The elder brother is angry
events.note: Verse 28 says only 'he'. Verse 25 identifies him as the elder son, and verses 26-27 explain why he became angry.

events.event: Abel keeps sheep and Cain tills the ground
events.note: Verse 2 states both occupations directly.

events.event: Both bring offerings to the LORD
events.note: Verses 3-4 describe Cain's and Abel's offerings.

events.event: God warns Cain that sin lieth at the door
events.note: Widened to include verse 6, which shows that the LORD is speaking to Cain.

events.event: Cain rises up against Abel in the field
events.note: Verse 8 describes the attack in the field.

events.event: God sets a mark upon Cain
events.note: Verse 15 says the LORD set a mark upon Cain.

events.event: God tells Abraham to take Isaac to the land of Moriah
events.note: Verse 2 holds the command, but the speaker is only called "he"; verse 1 shows that it is God tempting Abraham.

events.event: Abraham rises early and saddles his ass
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Isaac asks where the lamb is
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: The angel of the LORD calls out of heaven
events.note: Verse 10 adds the context: the call comes as Abraham takes the knife to slay his son.

events.event: A ram caught in a thicket is offered instead
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Pharaoh orders every son born to be cast into the river
events.note: The verse states Pharaoh's command in full.

events.event: Baby Moses is hidden in an ark of bulrushes
events.note: Widened to include verse 2, where his mother hides him for three months before making the ark. The name Moses is only given later, in Exodus 2:10.

events.event: Pharaoh's daughter finds the child
events.note: These verses fully show Pharaoh's daughter finding the child.

events.event: Moses flees to the land of Midian
events.note: The verse explicitly names Moses and Midian.

events.event: God speaks from the burning bush
events.note: These verses fully show the bush burning and God calling to Moses from it.

events.event: Israel camps before the mount
events.note: Keep: the verse shows Israel arriving in the desert of Sinai and camping before the mount.

events.event: Mount Sinai smokes as the LORD descends
events.note: Keep: the verse explicitly shows Mount Sinai smoking because the LORD descended on it in fire.

events.event: God speaks the ten commandments
events.note: Exodus 20:1-3 shows God speaking the opening commandments but never uses the phrase 'ten commandments'. Deuteronomy 4:13 names them as 'ten commandments' that God declared.

events.event: The people make a golden calf
events.note: Widened: verse 4 alone uses 'he' and 'them' (Aaron and the earrings). Verses 1-3 show the people demanding gods and bringing their gold.

events.event: Moses hews two new tables of stone
events.note: Widened: verse 1 only gives the LORD's command. Verse 4 records that Moses actually hewed the two tables.

events.event: Rahab hides the two spies
events.note: Verse 4 calls her only 'the woman'. Verse 1 names Rahab and the two spies, and verse 6 shows her hiding them under the flax on the roof.

events.event: Israel crosses the Jordan on dry ground
events.note: The current reference fully shows all Israel passing over Jordan on dry ground.

events.event: The people march around the city once a day for six days
events.note: Verse 14 begins with 'the second day'. Widening to verse 11 includes the first day's circuit, so the full six days of once-a-day marching are shown.

events.event: On the seventh day they compass the city seven times
events.note: The current reference fully shows the seven circuits on the seventh day.

events.event: The wall falls down flat
events.note: The current reference fully shows the shout, the trumpets and the wall falling down flat.

events.event: A little maid tells of the prophet in Samaria
events.note: Verse 2 introduces the little maid taken captive from Israel who waited on Naaman's wife. Verse 3 gives her words about the prophet in Samaria.

events.event: The king of Israel rends his clothes
events.note: Kept as is: the verse shows the king of Israel reading the letter and rending his clothes.

events.event: Elisha says to wash in Jordan seven times
events.note: Kept as is: Elisha sends a messenger telling him to wash in Jordan seven times.

events.event: Naaman turns away in a rage
events.note: Widened to include verse 11, which names Naaman as the one who was wroth and went away. Verse 12 ends with him turning away in a rage.

events.event: His flesh comes again like a little child's
events.note: Kept as is: he dips seven times in Jordan and his flesh comes again like that of a little child.

events.event: Hannah prays in bitterness of soul at Shiloh
events.note: Verse 10 names neither Hannah nor Shiloh. Verse 9 adds both, placing Hannah at Shiloh by the temple of the LORD.

events.event: Eli thinks she is drunken
events.note: Kept. This verse fully shows Hannah praying silently and Eli thinking she was drunken.

events.event: Hannah bears a son and names him Samuel
events.note: Kept. This verse fully shows Hannah bearing a son and naming him Samuel.

events.event: She lends the child to the LORD
events.note: Widened. Verses 26-27 show that Hannah is the speaker and that the child is the one she prayed for, which leads into her lending him to the LORD in verse 28.

events.event: Hannah prays: My heart rejoiceth in the LORD
events.note: Kept. This verse fully shows Hannah's prayer beginning 'My heart rejoiceth in the LORD.'

events.event: Nehemiah weeps over the news of Jerusalem
events.note: Verse 4 refers only to 'these words'. Verse 3 gives the news itself: the wall of Jerusalem is broken down and its gates are burned.

events.event: King Artaxerxes asks why his countenance is sad
events.note: The current reference names Artaxerxes and records his question about Nehemiah's sad countenance.

events.event: Nehemiah views the walls by night
events.note: The current reference shows Nehemiah going out by night and viewing the broken walls of Jerusalem.

events.event: Sanballat and Tobiah mock the builders
events.note: The current reference names both Sanballat and Tobiah and records their mocking.

events.event: The wall is finished in fifty and two days
events.note: The current reference states the wall was finished in fifty and two days.

events.event: A great multitude follows Jesus
events.note: Current reference fully shows the multitude following Jesus.

events.event: Jesus asks Philip where to buy bread
events.note: Current reference fully shows Jesus asking Philip.

events.event: Andrew tells Jesus of a lad with five barley loaves and two small fishes
events.note: Current reference fully shows Andrew's report of the lad.

events.event: The men sit down and Jesus gives thanks
events.note: Current reference fully shows the men sitting down and Jesus giving thanks.

events.event: Twelve baskets of fragments are gathered
events.note: Widened to include verse 12, where Jesus commands the fragments be gathered; verse 13 shows the twelve baskets filled.

events.event: Nebuchadnezzar sets up an image of gold
events.note: Verse 1 fully shows the king making and setting up the golden image in the plain of Dura.

events.event: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refuse to worship it
events.note: Verse 12 is the Chaldeans' accusation. Verses 16-18 add the three men's own refusal: they will not serve the king's gods nor worship the golden image.

events.event: The furnace is heated seven times hotter
events.note: Verse 19 fully shows the king commanding that the furnace be heated seven times more than usual.

events.event: The king sees four men loose in the fire
events.note: Verse 24 is added because verse 25 begins only with 'He answered'. Verse 24 names Nebuchadnezzar as the speaker and records his astonishment.

events.event: They come out with no smell of fire upon them
events.note: Verse 26 is added because it shows them coming forth from the fire. Verse 27 shows that no smell of fire had passed on them.

events.event: Zacchaeus, a chief among the publicans, seeks to see Jesus
events.note: Keep: names Zacchaeus as chief among the publicans and shows him seeking to see Jesus.

events.event: He climbs up into a sycomore tree
events.note: Keep: explicitly describes him climbing the sycomore tree.

events.event: Jesus says: to day I must abide at thy house
events.note: Keep: contains the quoted words.

events.event: The people murmur
events.note: Keep: states that they all murmured.

events.event: Zacchaeus gives half his goods to the poor
events.note: Keep: Zacchaeus declares he gives half his goods to the poor. The verse records his declaration rather than narrating the act itself.

events.event: The sisters send word that Lazarus is sick
events.note: Verse 3 does not name Lazarus or the sisters, so it is widened to verses 1-2, which identify Lazarus, Mary and Martha.

events.event: Jesus arrives after Lazarus has lain in the grave four days
events.note: Verse 17 only says 'he', so it is widened to verse 14, where Jesus says plainly that Lazarus is dead.

events.event: Jesus says: I am the resurrection, and the life
events.note: The current reference fully shows the saying.

events.event: Jesus weeps
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Lazarus comes forth bound with graveclothes
events.note: Verse 44 does not name Lazarus, so it is widened to verse 43, where Jesus cries 'Lazarus, come forth.'

events.event: Saul consents to Stephen's death
events.note: Acts 8:1 says only 'his death'. Acts 7:58-60 names Stephen and shows Saul present at the stoning.

events.event: A light from heaven shines around Saul near Damascus
events.note: Saul is named in Acts 9:1, and his journey to Damascus is set up in 9:2. Verse 3 alone says only 'he'.

events.event: Saul is three days without sight
events.note: Saul is named in Acts 9:8, which also shows him blinded and led into Damascus.

events.event: Ananias lays his hands on Saul
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event and names both Ananias and Saul.

events.event: Saul preaches Christ in the synagogues
events.note: Saul is named in Acts 9:19. Verse 20 alone says only 'he'.

events.event: Lot chooses the plain of Jordan
events.note: Verse 11 states directly that Lot chose the plain of Jordan and journeyed east.

events.event: Abram hears that Lot was taken captive
events.note: Verse 14 calls the captive only 'his brother'. Verse 12 names Lot as the one taken from Sodom, and verse 13 shows the news reaching Abram.

events.event: Two angels come to Sodom at evening
events.note: Verse 1 fully shows the two angels arriving at Sodom at even.

events.event: Lot's wife looks back
events.note: Verse 26 says only 'his wife'. Widening to verses 23-26 names Lot and shows that she looked back as Sodom was destroyed.

events.event: Jacob waters Rachel's flock at the well
events.note: Verse 9 shows the flock is the one Rachel kept; verse 10 shows Jacob rolling away the stone and watering it.

events.event: Jacob serves seven years for Rachel
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Jacob finds he has married Leah
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Jacob serves seven more years
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Ten brothers go down to buy corn in Egypt
events.note: The verse directly states that Joseph's ten brethren went down to buy corn in Egypt.

events.event: Simeon is bound before their eyes
events.note: Joseph takes Simeon and binds him before their eyes.

events.event: The brothers take Benjamin down to Egypt
events.note: The men take Benjamin, go down to Egypt and stand before Joseph.

events.event: The cup is found in Benjamin's sack
events.note: The search ends with the cup found in Benjamin's sack.

events.event: Joseph makes himself known
events.note: Verse 1 says Joseph made himself known. Verse 3 adds his actual words, "I am Joseph," so the revelation is shown in full.

events.event: Moses sends the spies to search Canaan
events.note: Moses sends them to spy out the land of Canaan.

events.event: Two men carry a cluster of grapes on a staff
events.note: At the brook of Eshcol they carry the cluster between two upon a staff.

events.event: Caleb says, Let us go up at once
events.note: Caleb's words are quoted exactly.

events.event: The people murmur against Moses and Aaron
events.note: All the children of Israel murmur against Moses and Aaron.

events.event: Israel must wander forty years
events.note: Widened to include verse 33, which uses the word 'wander' ("your children shall wander in the wilderness forty years"). Verse 34 gives the reason: a year for each day.

events.event: Balaam saddles his ass and goes with the princes of Moab
events.note: Current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: The ass sees the angel standing in the way
events.note: Current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: The LORD opens the mouth of the ass
events.note: Current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: The LORD opens Balaam's eyes
events.note: Current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Balak complains that Balaam has blessed Israel
events.note: Current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Abraham sends his servant to his kindred
events.note: Widened to include verse 2, which shows Abraham speaking to his servant. Verse 4 alone does not show who is being sent.

events.event: Rebekah offers to water the camels
events.note: Widened so Rebekah is named (verse 15). Verse 19 alone says only 'she.'

events.event: Laban runs out to the man at the well
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event and names Laban.

events.event: Rebekah says, I will go
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Rebekah becomes Isaac's wife
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Deborah judges Israel under the palm tree
events.note: Current reference fully shows Deborah judging Israel under the palm tree.

events.event: Deborah calls Barak to Mount Tabor
events.note: Current reference fully shows Deborah calling Barak and the command to draw toward mount Tabor.

events.event: Barak goes down from Mount Tabor
events.note: Current reference fully shows Barak going down from mount Tabor.

events.event: Jael drives a nail through Sisera's temples
events.note: Sisera is named in Judges 4:17-18, but verse 21 clearly shows the act itself. Kept as is.

events.event: Deborah and Barak sing a song
events.note: Widened to include the opening of the song itself.

events.event: David sees a woman from the roof
events.note: The verse fully shows David on the roof seeing the woman washing herself. Her name, Bathsheba, is given in the next verse (11:3), but the event as described does not need it.

events.event: David writes to set Uriah in the hottest battle
events.note: Verse 14 adds that David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah. Verse 15 gives the letter's words about the hottest battle.

events.event: Nathan says, Thou art the man
events.note: The verse contains Nathan's words exactly as described.

events.event: David confesses, I have sinned
events.note: The verse contains David's confession and Nathan's reply.

events.event: Solomon is born
events.note: The verse records the birth and naming of Solomon to David and Bathsheba.

events.event: Hezekiah breaks the brasen serpent
events.note: Verse 4 says only 'he', so it is widened back to verse 1, where Hezekiah is named.

events.event: Sennacherib comes up against the fenced cities of Judah
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Hezekiah spreads the letter before the LORD
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: The angel of the LORD strikes the Assyrian camp
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Sennacherib is slain by his sons in his own temple
events.note: Verse 37 says only 'he', so verse 36 is added to name Sennacherib. The 'temple' is the house of Nisroch his god.

events.event: Josiah becomes king at eight years old
events.note: The verse states directly that Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign.

events.event: The book of the law is found in the temple
events.note: Hilkiah finds the book of the law in the house of the LORD.

events.event: Josiah tears his clothes
events.note: Verse 10 shows Shaphan reading the book to the king, which sets up Josiah renting his clothes in verse 11.

events.event: Josiah makes a covenant before the LORD
events.note: The king stands by a pillar and makes a covenant before the LORD.

events.event: Josiah commands the people to keep the passover
events.note: The king commands all the people to keep the passover.

events.event: Absalom steals the hearts of the men of Israel
events.note: Widened so the passage shows what 'on this manner' means: Absalom intercepting petitioners at the gate and flattering them.

events.event: David flees from Jerusalem
events.note: Verse 14 gives only David's command to flee. Verse 16 records the king actually going forth with his household.

events.event: Absalom's head is caught in an oak
events.note: Current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Joab thrusts three darts into Absalom
events.note: Current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: David weeps, O my son Absalom
events.note: Current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: The elders ask Samuel for a king
events.note: Verse 4 shows that the speakers are the elders of Israel gathered to Samuel at Ramah. Verse 5 gives their request for a king.

events.event: Saul, a choice young man, is introduced
events.note: Verse 1 introduces Kish, the 'he' of verse 2, so players can see whose son Saul is.

events.event: Samuel anoints Saul with a vial of oil
events.note: Saul is not named in 10:1. Adding 9:27 shows that Samuel is speaking with Saul just before the anointing.

events.event: The people shout, God save the king
events.note: Saul is not named in verse 24. Verses 21-23 show Saul being chosen and brought before the people before they shout.

events.event: Samuel tells Saul the LORD has rejected him
events.note: Verse 22 shows that Samuel is the speaker. Verse 23 gives the rejection.

events.event: Jairus falls at Jesus' feet
events.note: Verse 22 names Jairus and shows him falling at Jesus' feet; verse 23 adds his plea for his dying daughter.

events.event: A woman touches Jesus' garment
events.note: Verse 27 shows the touch; the surrounding verses introduce the woman with the issue of blood and explain why she touched his garment.

events.event: Jesus asks, Who touched my clothes?
events.note: Verse 30 fully shows Jesus asking the question.

events.event: Messengers say, Thy daughter is dead
events.note: Verse 35 fully shows the messengers' report.

events.event: Jesus says, Talitha cumi
events.note: Verse 41 contains the words; verse 42 shows the damsel arising.

events.event: Cyrus makes a proclamation
events.note: Verse 1 breaks off at "saying,"; verses 2-3 give the content of Cyrus's proclamation about building the house of the LORD in Jerusalem.

events.event: The foundation of the temple is laid
events.note: Verse 10 shows the builders laying the foundation; verse 11 adds the people's shout of praise because the foundation was laid.

events.event: The people of the land trouble the builders
events.note: Verse 4 shows the troubling; verse 5 adds the hired counsellors who frustrated their purpose, which completes the sentence.

events.event: The house of God is finished
events.note: Verse 14 shows the elders building and finishing the work; verse 15 gives the completion date.

events.event: Ezra goes up from Babylon
events.note: Fully shows Ezra going up from Babylon.

events.event: Jesus goes up a mountain to pray
events.note: Verse 23 states that he went up into a mountain apart to pray, which fully shows the event.

events.event: The ship is tossed with waves
events.note: Verse 24 describes the ship in the midst of the sea, tossed with waves.

events.event: Jesus comes walking on the sea
events.note: Verse 25 says Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea, in the fourth watch of the night.

events.event: Peter begins to sink and cries, Lord, save me
events.note: Verse 30 alone says only 'he', so verses 28-29 are added to name Peter and show him walking on the water before he begins to sink.

events.event: The wind ceases when they come into the ship
events.note: Verse 32 states that the wind ceased when they were come into the ship.

events.event: Elisha asks for a double portion of Elijah's spirit
events.note: The current verse fully shows Elisha's request for a double portion.

events.event: Elisha divides the Jordan with Elijah's mantle
events.note: Verse 13 names Jordan as the place where Elisha stood. Verse 14 shows him smiting the waters with Elijah's mantle and the waters parting.

events.event: The widow's oil flows until the vessels are full
events.note: Verse 1 identifies the woman as a widow. Verses 2-6 show the oil being poured until the vessels were full and the oil stayed.

events.event: The Shunammite's son sneezes seven times
events.note: Verse 35 shows the child sneezing seven times. Verse 36 identifies the mother as the Shunammite and shows her son restored to her.

events.event: The axe head swims
events.note: Verse 5 shows the axe head falling into the water. Verse 6 alone mentions only 'the iron', so verse 5 is needed to show it was the axe head.

events.event: Peter says he is ready to go to prison and to death
events.note: Verse 33 does not name the speaker; verse 34, where Jesus answers 'I tell thee, Peter', shows that Peter is speaking.

events.event: Peter follows afar off
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Peter says, Woman, I know him not
events.note: Widened so Peter is named (v. 55) and the maid who challenges him is shown (v. 56).

events.event: The Lord turns and looks upon Peter
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Peter goes out and weeps bitterly
events.note: The current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Herod kills James with the sword
events.note: Widened to include verse 1, which names Herod the king; verse 2 alone says only "he".

events.event: Peter sleeps between two soldiers
events.note: This verse fully shows Peter sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains.

events.event: The chains fall off Peter's hands
events.note: This verse fully shows the angel raising Peter and his chains falling from his hands.

events.event: The iron gate opens of its own accord
events.note: This verse fully shows the iron gate opening "of his own accord".

events.event: Rhoda is too glad to open the gate
events.note: Widened to include verse 13, which names Rhoda; verse 14 alone says only "she".

events.event: An angel sends Philip toward the south
events.note: The verse fully shows the angel directing Philip south toward Gaza.

events.event: Philip meets a man of Ethiopia
events.note: Widened to verse 28, which shows the eunuch sitting in his chariot reading Esaias as Philip comes upon him.

events.event: Philip asks, Understandest thou what thou readest?
events.note: Verse 29 adds the Spirit telling Philip to join the chariot; verse 30 contains the question.

events.event: Philip baptizes the eunuch
events.note: The verse fully shows Philip baptizing the eunuch.

events.event: The Spirit of the Lord catches Philip away
events.note: The verse fully shows the Spirit catching Philip away.

events.event: Cornelius sees an angel in a vision
events.note: Verse 3 fully shows Cornelius seeing an angel of God in a vision.

events.event: Peter sees a great sheet let down from heaven
events.note: Verse 11 does not name Peter. Verses 9-10 show that it is Peter, praying on the housetop and falling into a trance.

events.event: Cornelius waits with his kinsmen and friends
events.note: Verse 24 fully shows Cornelius waiting with his kinsmen and near friends.

events.event: The Holy Ghost falls on all who hear
events.note: Verse 44 fully shows the Holy Ghost falling on all who heard while Peter spoke.

events.event: Peter commands them to be baptized
events.note: Verse 48 says only 'he'. Verses 46-47 name Peter and give his words about water for baptism.

events.event: The Lord opens Lydia's heart
events.note: The verse names Lydia and says the Lord opened her heart, so the current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: Paul casts the spirit out of a damsel
events.note: Verse 18 says only 'her'. The damsel with a spirit of divination is introduced in verse 16, so the passage is widened to include her.

events.event: Paul and Silas are cast into prison
events.note: Verse 23 says only 'them'. Verse 19 names Paul and Silas, and verse 24 shows them thrust into the inner prison.

events.event: At midnight they pray and sing praises
events.note: The verse names Paul and Silas, the midnight hour, and their praying and singing, so the current reference fully shows the event.

events.event: The jailer and all his household are baptized
events.note: Verse 33 says only 'he'. Verse 27 identifies the keeper of the prison, and verses 30-33 show his conversion and the baptism of him and all his household.

events.event: Stephen is chosen among the seven
events.note: Verse 3 sets out the choosing of seven men, and verse 5 names Stephen first among them.

events.event: Stephen does great wonders among the people
events.note: The current verse fully shows the event.

events.event: Stephen is brought to the council
events.note: Widened because verse 12 says only 'him'. Verses 9-10 name Stephen and show the dispute that led to his arrest.

events.event: Stephen sees the heavens opened
events.note: Widened to include verse 55, where he looks up steadfastly into heaven and sees the glory of God before he speaks.

events.event: Stephen prays, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge
events.note: Widened to include verse 59, which names Stephen as he is stoned and calling upon God.
